target.title: fix(mattermost): cap outbound target caches to prevent unbounded memory growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Mattermost-connected OpenClaw processes gradually accumulate unbounded heap memory proportional to the number of unique users, channel names, and DM pairs they have ever addressed. On active servers with many distinct recipients the four module-level Maps in `send.ts` — `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` — grow without limit and are never evicted.

**Concrete example:** An OpenClaw instance routing messages to 5 000 distinct Mattermost users over a week records 5 000 entries in `userByNameCache` and another 5 000 in `dmChannelCache`. No TTL, no eviction, no bound — every unique `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple stays in memory for the life of the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added four named cap constants and one `pruneMapToMaxSize` call after each cache `.set()`. `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) evicts the oldest insertion-order entry whenever the map exceeds its limit — the same LRU-like strategy used in `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

Cap values follow the existing Slack precedent (`SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX = 1024` at `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49`):

| Cache | Cap |
|---|---|
| `botUserCache` | 64 (bounded by distinct bot accounts) |
| `userByNameCache` | 512 |
| `channelByNameCache` | 512 |
| `dmChannelCache` | 1024 |

## User Impact

**Before:** Memory in the Mattermost send path grows linearly with the number of unique targets seen since process start. Operators on large servers must restart periodically to reclaim memory.

**After:** Each outbound cache is capped; the total overhead per cache is bounded and stable under sustained traffic.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:70–73` — four unbounded `Map` declarations, no cap or TTL before this PR
- `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49,572–578` — direct Slack precedent with `SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` implementation; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` re-exports it
- Diff: production change is +13 lines in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts`; call-site regressions added in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts`

### Behavior proof

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
```

New regressions in `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.test.ts` assert outbound caches stay bounded:

- `evicts oldest DM channel cache entries after the configured cap` — 1025 distinct `user:` sends force a cache miss on the first entry after the 1024 cap.
- `evicts oldest user-by-name cache entries after the configured cap` — 513 distinct `@username` sends force a username re-lookup for the first entry after the 512 cap.

This mirrors the Slack DM cache precedent and reuses the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper contract from `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

---

> **AI-assisted PR** — Generated with Cursor/Claude. Logic verified against `src/infra/map-size.ts` and `extensions/slack/src/send.ts` precedent. Diff is minimal and non-breaking: existing callers are unaffected, cache semantics are preserved, only the maximum retained size changes.

target.title: [AI] fix(memory): use truncateUtf16Safe for dreaming snippet truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`dreaming-phases.ts` truncates user-generated snippet text with `.slice(0, 280)`, which splits UTF-16 surrogate pairs. When an emoji straddles the 280-char boundary, `.slice()` produces a lone surrogate (`\ud83d`) that renders as `�` in daily memory headings and session corpus snippets.

- **Problem**: 5 `.slice(0, N)` call sites on user-facing text can split surrogate pairs at the truncation boundary
- **Solution**: Replace with `truncateUtf16Safe()` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, the standard SDK helper
- **What changed**: `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts` (+6/-5 — add import, 5 call sites)
- **What did NOT change**: Truncation limits (280/344 chars), whitespace normalization, heading extraction logic

## Why This Change Was Made

Daily dreaming headings, session corpus snippets, and citation text can contain emoji from user conversations. When truncation splits a surrogate pair, the resulting `�` corrupts the stored snippet. `truncateUtf16Safe` is already used in `session-cost-usage.ts`, `cron`, `exec-approval`, and `node-host` modules for the same purpose.

## User Impact

Users with emoji near the 280-char boundary in dreaming headings or session snippets will no longer see `�` replacement characters in stored memory content.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Dreaming snippet truncation no longer splits surrogate pairs at the boundary
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/dreaming-emoji-safe-truncation`

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice';
const heading = '📊'.repeat(140); // 280 chars, emoji at boundary
console.log('BEFORE .slice(0,280):', JSON.stringify(heading.slice(0,280).slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(heading.slice(0,280)));
console.log('AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe:', JSON.stringify(truncateUtf16Safe(heading,280).slice(-10)), 'lone surrogate:', /[\uD800-\uDBFF](?![\uDC00-\uDFFF])/.test(truncateUtf16Safe(heading,280)));
"

BEFORE .slice(0,280): "📊📊📊📊📊\ud83d" lone surrogate: true
AFTER  truncateUtf16Safe: "📊📊📊📊📊📊" lone surrogate: false
```

- **Observed result after fix**: Truncation counts full code points; emoji at the boundary remain intact
- **What was not tested**: Live dreaming ingest with real workspace content containing complex emoji (ZWJ sequences)

## Regression Test Plan

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)
```

target.title: fix: remove phantom UND_ERR_CONNECT error code
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`UND_ERR_CONNECT` is used as an error code in two subsystems but has never existed in undici. The real connect-phase error code is `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`.

Dead error codes are not harmless — they create a correctness risk: if a future version of undici introduces `UND_ERR_CONNECT` with different semantics (e.g., a non-transient connect failure), the existing code would silently misclassify it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`UND_ERR_CONNECT` appears in 5 locations across 2 files. Each match is against a Set or regex that classifies transient network errors for gateway crash decisions or retry logic. Since the code can never match, the entry is dead — but removing it prevents future misclassification if undici ever adds this error.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `b341c334` on branch `fix/remove-und-err-connect-phantom`.

### undici source: no `UND_ERR_CONNECT` exists

```
$ grep -rn "UND_ERR_" node_modules/undici/lib/ --include="*.js" | grep -o "UND_ERR_[A-Z_]*" | sort -u

UND_ERR_ABORT
UND_ERR_ABORTED
UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT
UND_ERR_BPL_MISSING_UPSTREAM
UND_ERR_CLOSED
UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT    ← only connect-phase timeout code
UND_ERR_DESTROYED
UND_ERR_HEADERS_OVERFLOW
UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT
UND_ERR_HTTP_PARSER
UND_ERR_INFO
UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG
UND_ERR_INVALID_RETURN_VALUE
UND_ERR_MAX_ORIGINS_REACHED
UND_ERR_NOT_SUPPORTED
UND_ERR_PRX_TLS
UND_ERR_REQ_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH
UND_ERR_REQ_RETRY
UND_ERR_RES_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH
UND_ERR_RES_EXCEEDED_MAX_SIZE
UND_ERR_RESPONSE
UND_ERR_SOCKET
UND_ERR_SOCKS
UND_ERR_WS_MESSAGE_SIZE_EXCEEDED
```

### Codebase usage: 5 sites across 2 files

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES Set (controls whether an unhandled rejection crashes the gateway):

```diff
 const TRANSIENT_NETWORK_CODES = new Set([
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "UND_ERR_SOCKET",
```

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — BENIGN_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_NETWORK_CODES Set:

```diff
 const BENIGN_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION_NETWORK_CODES = new Set([
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "ERR_HTTP2_INVALID_SESSION",
```

**`src/infra/unhandled-rejections.ts`** — Two regex patterns for matching error codes in log messages. `|UND_ERR_CONNECT|` removed from the alternation in both.

**`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.ts`** — Retry error code Set (controls whether an API request is retried):

```diff
   "UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT",
   "UND_ERR_DNS_RESOLVE_FAILED",
-  "UND_ERR_CONNECT",
   "UND_ERR_SOCKET",
```

### Impact analysis

| Scenario | Before (with phantom) | After (removed) |
|----------|----------------------|-----------------|
| Any real undici error code | Matches via its real entry (e.g. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`) | Same match, unchanged |
| If undici adds `UND_ERR_CONNECT` in the future | Possibly misclassified as transient/retryable | Falls through to default handling, safer |
| Current runtime behavior | Never matches (code does not exist) | No change |

All real undici error codes continue to match correctly. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, and every other real code are untouched.

## User Impact

No behavioral change. The code being removed has never matched any real error.

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — dead code removal.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — error classification internals only.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. All real error codes remain unchanged.
- **Mitigation:** Verified against undici source at `node_modules/undici/lib/`. The dependent error codes (`UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `UND_ERR_SOCKET`, etc.) are untouched and confirmed present.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap at the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn — identical fix.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge**:

Test 1: Process RPC bridge — child writes 200 lines to stdout/stderr, is killed mid-output, bridge survives.
Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge — real `http/request` to `https://httpbin.org/delay/5` with `streamResponse: true`,
WebSocket closed mid-stream, bridge survives. The HTTP test exercises the full `http.ts` subprocess path:

target.title: Dashboard: ops widgets — agent status + approvals queue
target.body:
> The operational half of the builtin set: see what every agent is doing, and act on what's waiting for you — from a dashboard cell.

Closes #101145 and #101144. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `agent-status.ts` + `approvals.ts` and their wiring as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**`builtin:agent-status` (#101145)** — a compact per-agent/session status list: active-run vs idle, current label, and freshness — the "what's everything doing right now?" glance. It binds to the same `sessions.list` data the `sessions` builtin already uses (no new backend), so it live-updates on the existing broadcast path.

**`builtin:approvals` (#101144)** — a pending-approvals queue with Approve/Deny actions, wired end-to-end through the **existing** widget-approval infrastructure from #101098 (`dashboard.widget.approve`): pending `custom:` widgets appear as cards, and a decision dispatches the same client path the Workspaces pending-card uses. The queue arrives via a new `ctx.approvals` source on the builtin context (mirroring the existing `ctx.embed` pattern), because it's in-memory workspace state rather than an RPC binding.

**Scope note (deliberate):** the gateway's exec/plugin approval RPCs (`exec.approval.*`, `plugin.approval.*`) exist and the app shell uses them, but they are operator-scoped and not in the dashboard's read-only binding allowlist (`DATA_READ_RPC_ALLOWLIST`). Widening that allowlist is a security decision we didn't want to smuggle into a widget PR — so this widget covers the dashboard's own approval queue today, and is shaped to take exec/plugin approvals as additional sources the moment maintainers bless that allowlist addition (called out in the module header). That keeps #72545 progressing without expanding any privilege surface.

## How it works
Both widgets follow the established builtin contract (`renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult`), registered in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` + `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN`. Agent-status is a pure mapper over the resolved `sessions.list` value. Approvals renders from `ctx.approvals` (built by the dashboard view from workspace state) and dispatches decisions through the existing, already-authorized `dashboard.widget.approve` method — this PR adds **no new gateway method and no new privilege**.

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** There's no cross-agent activity view in the dashboard (#101145 / the #39127–#54577 cluster), and approvals had no dashboard surface (#101144, advancing #72545) — operators had to open each session or wait for the pending-card to appear on the Workspaces tab. This adds two operational builtins: a live agent-status list and an approvals queue with working Approve/Deny.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 100 passed, including the new suites (status derivation filters + provenance, decision-vocabulary mapping + limit, populated/empty renders, and Approve/Deny wiring asserted against a mocked client dispatching `dashboard.widget.approve`); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean; `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` green (schema kind additions).

target.title: Fix/parse keyed answers url scheme split
target.body: Closes #101722 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where users answering a multi-question agent prompt with a bare URL (e.g. `https://example.com`) would receive a corrupted answer when the question id matched the URL scheme. `parseKeyedAnswers` split the URL on the first colon and stored a stray key `https` with value `//example.com`, causing the agent to receive the truncated value instead of the full URL. ## Why This Change Was Made Added a negative lookahead `(?!\/\/)` after the separator character so colon-slash-slash sequences are never treated as key-value delimiters. URLs embedded in keyed answers (e.g. `endpoint: https://example.com`) were already handled correctly by the existing lazy value capture - only bare URL lines produced stray keys. ## User Impact Agent questions that receive bare URL answers in multi-question prompts no longer risk returning a truncated value when the question id matches the URL scheme name. ## Evidence Before fix - `parseKeyedAnswers` on `https://example.com\n8080` produced stray key `https → //example.com`. A question with id `https` received `//example.com` instead of the full URL. After fix - no stray key is created. The fallback line correctly returns `https://example.com`.

target.title: improve(diagnostics-otel): make agent-duration histograms usable beyond 10s
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `openclaw.run.duration_ms`, `openclaw.harness.duration_ms`, and
`openclaw.context.tokens` histograms used the OTel SDK default bucket
boundaries. The default duration buckets top out at 10s, but agent runs
routinely take minutes — so nearly every run lands in the `+Inf` overflow
bucket. Anyone reading p50/p95/p99 latency for agent runs sees a flat,
meaningless distribution unless they reconfigure buckets at the collector.

## Why This Change Was Made

Attach `explicit_bucket_boundaries` advice via named constants, matching the
existing `GEN_AI_*_BUCKETS` convention already in this file:
- `AGENT_DURATION_MS_BUCKETS` (1s … 1h) for the run and harness duration
  histograms, which share the same latency range.
- `CONTEXT_TOKENS_BUCKETS` for the small-integer context-size histogram.

Histogram bucket advice only affects how new data is aggregated; it changes
no recorded values and no public API.

## User Impact

Operators get meaningful latency percentiles for agent runs and harness
lifecycle out of the box, across the full seconds-to-an-hour range, without
any collector-side bucket configuration.

## Evidence

- New unit test asserts all three histograms advertise the expected bucket
  boundaries and that run/harness share the same set.
- `extensions/diagnostics-otel` test suite: **96 passed**.
- Typecheck (`tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`), lint

target.title: fix: keep task title truncation UTF-16 safe in restart/diagnostic output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway restart blocker diagnostics, gateway reload logs, and CLI run-loop output could display broken U+FFFD replacement characters when a task title contained an emoji or CJK supplementary character at the 80-character truncation boundary.

Three identical copies of `formatTaskBlocker` share the same `task.title.slice(0, 80)` pattern, which cuts at UTF-16 code unit boundaries. Emoji like 🚀 are surrogate pairs (2 code units) and get split.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `task.title.slice(0, 80)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(task.title, 80)` in all three files, matching the existing UTF-16-safe truncation pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase.

## User Impact

Task title text in gateway restart diagnostics, reload logs, and CLI run-loop output now displays cleanly truncated text without broken characters.

## Evidence

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli/task-title-truncate-utf16.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Standalone production-path proof

Exercises the exact changed `createSafeGatewayRestartPreflight → formatTaskBlocker` code path with an emoji crossing the 80-code-unit truncation boundary:

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-task-title-utf16-safe.mjs
node=v22.22.0
head=80656a568479dccb521170410496a3272dd201fd
function=createSafeGatewayRestartPreflight → formatTaskBlocker
titleCodeUnits=81
rawSliceCharAt79=U+d83d
beforeFix_loneHighSurrogate=true
blockerMessage=taskId=proof-task-1 status=running runtime=subagent title=ttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttttt
afterFix_hasLoneSurrogate=false
result=PASS
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `formatTaskBlocker` output contains no lone surrogate when the task title places an emoji across the 80-code-unit truncation boundary. The safe-truncated title (79 't' chars) is cleanly emitted.
- **Before behavior:** raw `slice(0, 80)` includes a lone high surrogate (U+D83D) which renders as U+FFFD in terminal/log output.
- **After behavior:** `truncateUtf16Safe` backs off to 79 code units before the surrogate pair, producing clean diagnostic output.

### Files Changed (5 files, +28/-4)

```
 scripts/proof-task-title-utf16-safe.mjs                     | 66 +++++++
 src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.ts                             |  3 +-
 src/cli/gateway-cli/task-title-truncate-utf16.test.ts       | 33 ++++-
 src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.ts                       |  3 +-
 src/infra/restart-coordinator.ts                            |  3 +-
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)
Yes. Gateway restart/reload diagnostic messages and CLI run-loop drain output no longer emit U+FFFD for emoji-boundary task titles.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

What is the highest-risk area?
Gateway diagnostic/log string formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?
The patch is limited to three identical truncation boundaries, reuses an existing internal helper with established test coverage, and adds focused regression coverage that exercises the `createSafeGatewayRestartPreflight` production path.

target.title: fix(agents): strip leaked truncation sentinels from final replies (#82121)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Internal truncation sentinels such as `...(truncated)...`, `[... N more characters truncated]` (with or without the live `; rerun with narrower args if needed` hint), `...[truncated]...`, `...[additional startup memory truncated]...`, and `…[truncated]` could leak into final user-facing assistant replies. The central sanitizer already strips other internal artifacts, but it did not recognize truncation markers, so users could receive implementation-only truncation text as if it were part of the answer.

## Why This Change Was Made
The root cause is in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: `sanitizeUserFacingText()` had no truncation-sentinel stripping step. Producers such as tool-result context guards, tool-transcript truncation, startup context truncation, post-compaction context truncation, and `formatContextLimitTruncationNotice()` can emit these markers; if any marker reaches final reply text, the sanitizer previously passed it through unchanged.

This follows the conservative direction from clawsweeper's review on #82121: "Add a focused final-text sanitizer rule for standalone or trailing truncation sentinel lines, with regression tests that preserve inline prose and code examples; producer-only changes would leave other sentinel sources uncovered."

Per clawsweeper's producer-coverage finding on this PR, the sentinel set now also matches the live context-limit notice emitted by `formatContextLimitTruncationNotice()` — `[... N more characters truncated; rerun with narrower args if needed]` — with the hint as an optional suffix so older bare payloads replayed from stored sessions are still stripped. The regression asserts against the real producer output (imports `formatContextLimitTruncationNotice`), so future format drift breaks the test instead of silently un-covering the notice.

## User Impact
Final assistant replies no longer expose OpenClaw's internal truncation markers, including the live context-limit notice with the rerun hint. The sanitizer only strips a fixed set of precise sentinel shapes when they occupy a standalone line or trail at the very end of the reply, so normal prose, code snippets, JSON values, and unrelated bracketed text (e.g. a differently-phrased `[... 7 more characters truncated; see the log for details]`) remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Changes
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/sanitize-user-facing-text.ts`: adds `stripTruncationSentinels()` to the sanitizer pipeline before error-context classification; sentinel set covers the live rerun-hint notice variant.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.sanitizeuserfacingtext.test.ts`: regression coverage for standalone/trailing sentinels, the live rerun-hint notice (asserted against the real producer function), and preservation of inline prose/code/JSON and differently-phrased brackets.

## Evidence
All proof below is from current head `4a08d7178d`, rebased on `upstream/main` (`99b24e7416`), run on Node v24.4.0 (previous rounds ran on a below-floor Node; that caveat is gone).

Real module behavior — the actual `sanitizeUserFacingText()` fed the actual `formatContextLimitTruncationNotice()` output via `tsx`:

```text
node v24.4.0
RAW FINAL REPLY  : "Here is the summary you asked for.\n[... 5000 more characters truncated; rerun with narrower args if needed]"
SANITIZED OUTPUT : "Here is the summary you asked for."
```

Negative control — with the test present but the source fix reverted, the new regression fails on the unpatched tree, confirming it guards this exact gap:

```text
× strips the live context-limit notice with the rerun hint (#82121) 9ms
Tests  1 failed | 126 passed (127)
```

After fix:

```text

```

target.title: feat(signal): add setup wizard container flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where Signal setup required users to hand-configure native `signal-cli` even when they wanted OpenClaw to guide them through a local Signal REST container or an existing Signal API server. It also fixes setup/status gaps where Signal transport mode, receive readiness, and multi-account setup state could be misreported or persisted on the wrong account.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal setup now owns native, Docker container, and existing-server setup paths inside the Signal plugin, while core setup gains only the generic `setupApplied` rollback signal needed to avoid persisting failed or cancelled setup attempts. Managed Docker setup verifies the account-specific `/v1/receive/{account}` WebSocket before saving container setup, and the branch has been rebased onto current `main` while preserving current-main Signal container attachment hardening.

## User Impact

Users can configure Signal through the setup wizard with a Docker container flow, QR/linking guidance, and existing-server reconfiguration that does not require re-entering an already saved Signal number. Operators get clearer `channels status` output for ready, account-missing, receive-unavailable, and unreachable Signal states, and mixed multi-account configs keep transport fields scoped to the intended account.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- Docker setup verifies `/v1/receive/{account}` before every managed setup success return: single listed account, selected account from multiple linked accounts, and newly linked QR account.
- Non-interactive existing-server setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "auto"` and `autoStart: false`, so a previous container setup does not force a later `--http-url` config through the container adapter.
- Non-interactive native setup resets stale Docker transport state to `apiMode: "native"`, `autoStart: true`, and clears `httpUrl`, so a later `--cli-path`/host/port setup does not keep using an old external server.
- Failed or cancelled setup returns `setupApplied: false`, so core setup skips account selection hooks, setup callbacks, completion notes, and partial config persistence for unsuccessful setup attempts.
- Signal status/probe output exposes readiness-specific states instead of collapsing account-missing or receive-unavailable probes into generic working/unreachable output.
- Screenshots are omitted because this PR changes terminal/setup wizard and gateway status behavior; the reviewer-checkable proof is the command/test output and config transition coverage below.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression before provider execution
target.body:
Closes #101923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where large image files (e.g. phone photos exceeding 25 megapixels) sent through the media-understanding image description pipeline would trigger provider dimension limit errors such as "Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit". The image tool path already resized images before provider execution, but the media-understanding path — used for automatic attachment descriptions and the `infer image describe` CLI command — was not applying the shared compression ladder.

## Why This Change Was Made

The image tool and media-understanding subsystems evolved independently. PR #86037 introduced HEIC/HEIF format normalization for the media-understanding path but did not include dimension-based compression, while the image tool side gained compression through `loadWebMedia` with `imageCompression` policy in PR #85742. This gap affected three paths: configured media-understanding runs triggered by message attachments, `infer image describe` without `--model`, and `infer image describe --model`.

The fix adds a shared `compressImageForDescription()` utility that reads `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` and `agents.defaults.imageQuality` to build an `ImageCompressionPolicy` and runs it through the existing `optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia` resize ladder. It is called after HEIC normalization in both `runner.entries.ts` (the provider dispatch path) and `runtime.ts` (the CLI `prepareImageDescriptionInput` path). HEIC conversion and dimension compression remain separate concerns; no existing function signatures or public types were modified.

## User Impact

Users who configure `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` will now have their large image files automatically resized before provider execution in the media-understanding path, matching the behavior already present in the image tool. This prevents provider dimension limit errors when using `infer image describe` or when the agent automatically describes image attachments.

## Evidence

- 241 tests pass across 7 test files, including 9 new tests covering configuration combinations, dimension clamping, NaN/Infinity guards, and fractional value flooring
- `src/media-understanding/image-compression.test.ts` — 9/9 ✅
- `src/media-understanding/runtime.test.ts` — 21/21 ✅
- `src/media-understanding/runner.entries.guards.test.ts` — 12/12 ✅
- `src/media-understanding/media-understanding-misc.test.ts` — 19/19 ✅
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — 75/75 ✅
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts` — 94/94 ✅ (no regression)
- `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` — 106/106 ✅ (no regression)

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(cli): keep plugin description truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `formatPluginLine` could produce broken U+FFFD replacement characters when a plugin description contained an emoji or CJK supplementary character at the 57-character truncation boundary.

`plugin.description.slice(0, 57)` cuts at UTF-16 code unit boundaries — emoji like 🚀 are surrogate pairs (2 code units) and get split.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `plugin.description.slice(0, 57)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(plugin.description, 57)` in the non-verbose branch of `formatPluginLine`, matching the existing UTF-16-safe truncation pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase.

Scope: the exported `formatPluginLine` formatter (non-verbose path). The default `openclaw plugins list` table rendering path uses `splitGraphemes` (grapheme-safe) and does not truncate descriptions, so it is unaffected.

## User Impact

Consumers of `formatPluginLine` (including `openclaw plugins list --verbose`) with plugin descriptions containing emoji or CJK near the 60-character display limit now receive cleanly truncated text without replacement characters.

## Evidence

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-list-description-truncate-utf16.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

### Standalone production-path proof

Exercises the exact changed `formatPluginLine` code path with an emoji crossing the 57-code-unit truncation boundary:

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-plugins-list-utf16-safe.mjs
node=v22.22.0
head=16a44f9131f4cb0dde7ad056685c76a8e9a7965d
function=formatPluginLine(plugin, verbose=false)
descriptionCodeUnits=59
rawSliceCharAt56=U+d83d
beforeFix_loneHighSurrogate=true
afterFix_hasUFFFD=false
result=PASS
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `formatPluginLine` non-verbose output contains no U+FFFD replacement characters when the description places a surrogate pair across the 57-code-unit truncation boundary.
- **Before behavior:** raw `slice(0, 57)` includes a lone high surrogate (U+D83D) which renders as U+FFFD.
- **After behavior:** `truncateUtf16Safe` backs off to 56 code units before the surrogate pair, appends "...", producing clean output.

### Files Changed (3 files, +26/-2)

```
 src/cli/plugins-list-description-truncate-utf16.test.ts | 24 +++++++++++++++
 scripts/proof-plugins-list-utf16-safe.mjs               | 84 +++++++
 src/cli/plugins-list-format.ts                          |  4 +--
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)
Yes. `formatPluginLine` non-verbose output no longer emits U+FFFD for emoji-boundary descriptions.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)
No.

What is the highest-risk area?
CLI plugin list string formatting.

How is that risk mitigated?
The patch is limited to a single truncation boundary, reuses an existing internal helper with established test coverage, and adds focused regression coverage that exercises the exact changed formatter path.

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

Validated on the rebased head `5e5781ee41f99f172c537cbd64d44828d751a292`, based on current `origin/main` `6765eb0166fc2607203caf8ca3b96824b1352e10`:

- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter ChatTranscriptCacheStoreTests` (39 tests passed)
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter ChatTranscriptCache` (6 tests passed)
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayEndpointStoreTests` (33 tests passed)
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --product OpenClaw`
- `git diff --check`

This refresh is rebase-only over the existing one-file actor-isolation fix.

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, the persisted aborted session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once repeated automatic recovery has already shown that the session is wedged.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, which keeps the gateway focused on the same wedged session instead of leaving the row in a terminal state for operator inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR, but changes the policy to the maintainer-requested recovery-fuse model rather than a generic cross-boot retry counter:

- Main-session restart recovery now has its own optional `mainRestartRecovery` state, aligned with the existing subagent tombstone shape: `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Only accepted automatic resume dispatches charge the durable fuse. Transcript preflight failures, transcript read failures, and dispatch-before-acceptance failures do not consume the fuse.
- Two rapid accepted automatic recovery attempts within two minutes are allowed; the next rapid re-entry tombstones the row before dispatch, clears `abortedLastRun`, and transitions the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` stays a lifecycle-generation ignore list. For old released rows that only have repeated `restartRecoveryRuns` markers, recovery uses those markers only as a conservative compatibility floor, not as the canonical counter.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is no longer the durable cross-boot policy.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- The new persisted state is optional and scoped to automatic main-session restart recovery; existing rows do not need migration.
- This does not change credentials, auth, provider discovery, network behavior, public config defaults, wire protocol, Telegram/systemd runtime behavior, or lifecycle event suppression semantics.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime proof through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session can make two rapid accepted automatic recovery attempts, but the next rapid restart tombstones the row instead of repeatedly dispatching another resume. Deterministic transcript failures fail before charging that liveness fuse, so a bad transcript tail is not retried as if it were a transient gateway dispatch problem.

After inspection, `openclaw doctor --fix` can clear stale aborted recovery flags without deleting the tombstone metadata.

## Evidence

Issue-specific runtime proof through the production main-session restart-recovery entrypoint:

```text
Validation `post-commit-runtime-restart-recovery-tombstone-proof` (pass, exit_code=0)
[main-session-restart-recovery] tombstoned main-session restart recovery: agent:main:main (main-session restart recovery blocked after 2 rapid accepted resume attempts; run "openclaw doctor --fix" to clear stale restart-recovery flags after inspection)
proof exhausted-fuse: skipped=1, no resume dispatch path, durable tombstone persisted, terminal lifecycle closed
[main-session-restart-recovery] tombstoned main-session restart recovery: agent:main:main (main-session restart recovery blocked after 3 rapid accepted resume attempts; run "openclaw doctor --fix" to clear stale restart-recovery flags after inspection)
proof legacy-markers: old released row maps restartRecoveryRuns to a conservative tombstone gate before resume dispatch
[main-session-restart-recovery] marked interrupted main session failed: agent:main:main (transcript tail is not resumable)
[main-session-restart-recovery] main-session restart recovery complete: recovered=0 failed=1 skipped=0
proof preflight: non-resumable transcript fails before resume dispatch and does not charge durable fuse
runtime proof: restart-recovery durable fuse/tombstone and preflight boundaries verified on current local head
```

Focused regression coverage for the main-session restart-recovery policy and shared recovery helper:

```text
Validation `targeted-main-restart-recovery-tests` (pass, exit_code=0)
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 43 passed (43)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 16.17s

Validation `subagent-orphan-recovery-tests` (pass, exit_code=0)
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 19 passed (19)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.73s

Validation `doctor-state-integrity-main-tombstone-test-post-commit` (pass, exit_code=0)
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 34 passed (34)

```

Additional targeted regression coverage retained from this PR update:

```text
Validation `post-recreate-targeted-session-recovery-tests` (pass, exit_code=0)
Test Files 6 passed / Tests 470 passed
Test Files 2 passed / Tests 58 passed
Test Files 2 passed / Tests 91 passed
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards

Static checks on the current code diff:

Review finding disposition:

- Durable stop condition: main-session restart recovery now uses a dedicated `mainRestartRecovery` fuse/tombstone state instead of flat retry/quarantine fields.
- Retry semantics: the durable policy is two rapid accepted automatic recovery attempts within two minutes, not three cross-boot retries. In-process retry/backoff remains separate.
- Charging boundary: only accepted gateway resume dispatch records an automatic attempt. Transcript preflight/read failures and dispatch rejection before acceptance do not charge the durable fuse.
- Tombstone lifecycle: exhausted rows transition to `failed`, clear `abortedLastRun`, stamp `endedAt` and `runtimeMs`, and persist `wedgedAt` / `wedgedReason`.
- Legacy row compatibility: old rows with repeated `restartRecoveryRuns` and no `mainRestartRecovery` can still tombstone conservatively before dispatch, while `restartRecoveryRuns` remains a lifecycle event suppression list.

target.title: feat(chunking): enhance paragraph and table merging logic for QQ Bot
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves / 解决了什么问题

Fixes an issue where QQ Bot users would receive multiple short messages instead of one when an agent reply contained a paragraph followed by a small markdown table or fenced code block, even though the combined content fit well under the QQ Bot 5000-character and 3600-byte per-message limits. Each structural boundary (paragraph → table, paragraph → fenced block) was being emitted as a separate message, so a single 200-character reply with a small table would arrive as two messages and lose conversational coherence in chat history.

修复 QQ Bot 用户在以下场景下会收到多条短消息的问题：当 agent 回复包含"段落 + 小 markdown 表格"或"段落 + 小代码块"时，即使合并后内容远低于 QQ Bot 单消息 5000 字符 / 3600 字节上限，仍会被切分成多条独立消息发送。一个 200 字符的回复附带小表格会被切成两条消息，导致聊天记录中对话不连贯。

Affected surface: QQ Bot block-reply path (default `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`, `streaming: false`, or `streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`). C2C streaming path is intentionally untouched.

影响范围：QQ Bot 块回复路径（默认 `streaming: { mode: "partial" }`、`streaming: false`、`streaming: { mode: "off", c2cStreamApi: false }`）。C2C 流式路径不在本次改动范围。

## Why This Change Was Made / 为何做此修改

The QQ Bot markdown chunker (`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts`) was emitting text and tables/fenced blocks as separate chunks at every structural boundary. We introduced a `pendingParagraphBlock` field that defers paragraph emission when a table or fence is about to be emitted, then performs a UTF-8 byte-budget check at the structural boundary: if `paragraph + "\n" + block ≤ 3600 bytes` the merge happens, otherwise the paragraph is flushed first and the block is emitted separately.

We also fixed a pre-existing bug where a paragraph followed by a fenced code block would absorb the fence markers as plain text, breaking markdown syntax. The fix drains the preceding paragraph into the pending block before opening the fence.

Design boundaries:
- Byte budget kept at the existing `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600` (no new config surface).
- Outer 5000-character `textChunkLimit` and `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` unchanged.
- Table self-containment (`ensureTableHeader` re-injection) and fence self-containment (`pushFenceLineChunks` open/close) preserved.
- C2C streaming path (`StreamingController`) not modified.

我们在 `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.ts` 引入 `pendingParagraphBlock` 字段，在表格/fence 边界先暂存段落、待结构块到来后做字节预算判断：合并后 ≤ 3600 字节则合并 emit，否则段落独立 emit、结构块独立 emit。

同时修复了一个潜在 bug：原代码在"段落 → fence"边界会把 fence 标记当作普通文本吸收，破坏 markdown 语法。本次修复在 fence 起点先 drain 出前置段落再启动 fence。

设计边界：
- 字节预算沿用现有 `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT = 3600`（不新增 config）
- 外层 5000 字符 `textChunkLimit` / `TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` 不变
- 表格自包含（`ensureTableHeader` 重发 header）、fence 自包含（`pushFenceLineChunks` 开闭成对）保持不变
- C2C 流式路径（`StreamingController`）未修改

## User Impact / 用户影响

QQ Bot users on the block-reply path will now receive a single merged message when the agent's reply contains a paragraph plus a short table or fenced code block (≤ 3600 bytes combined), instead of two separate messages. Markdown structure is preserved in both merged and unmerged cases. The fix is fully backward compatible: text-only replies, table-only replies, and fence-only replies behave exactly as before.

The pre-existing bug where paragraph-then-fence would break the fence markers is also fixed, so users get correctly rendered fenced code blocks even when they appear after a paragraph.

块回复路径下，QQ Bot 用户在 agent 回复包含"段落 + 短表格/fence"时（合并 ≤ 3600 字节）会收到一条合并消息，而不是两条。合并和不合并两种情况下 markdown 结构都正确保留。本次修改完全向后兼容：纯文本、纯表格、纯 fence 的行为与之前一致。

段落后接 fence 时 fence 标记被破坏的预存 bug 也一并修复，用户可以正确收到 fence 包裹的代码块。

## Evidence / 验证

### Unit tests

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
   Duration  ~290ms
```

New test cases added (9):
- `merges a short paragraph with a short table when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `merges a short paragraph with a short fenced block when total bytes fit the QQ limit`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a table that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `does not merge a paragraph with a fenced block that would push the chunk past 3600 bytes`
- `emits only prose unchanged when no table or fence is present`
- `emits only a table unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits only a fenced block unchanged when no surrounding prose exists`
- `emits a paragraph with no trailing table or fence inside chunkText itself`
- `falls back to the base chunker when a single oversized paragraph exceeds 3600 bytes`

Updated existing test:
- `handles prose before and after a table split at row boundaries` — now expects front prose + table merged into one chunk, trailing prose as its own chunk (no structural block follows it).

### Plugin-wide regression check

```
$ pnpm test extensions/qqbot
 Test Files  69 passed (69)
      Tests  602 passed (602)

target.title: fix(launcher): stop respawned children after parent death on Unix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #79534. When `openclaw.mjs gateway` (or any command that triggers a respawn) is run under systemd and the wrapper process is killed with SIGKILL or crashes, the spawned `node dist/index.js ...` child can survive and become an orphan reparented to PID 1. The orphan keeps ports bound, so systemd restarts fail with `EADDRINUSE` and the unit enters a crash loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launcher already forwards catchable signals (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT) to respawn children, but SIGKILL and wrapper crashes cannot run that forwarding path. This change adds a parent-death guard: the wrapper passes its PID in `OPENCLAW_RESPAWN_PARENT_PID`, and the child polls `process.ppid` on Unix; if the child is reparented, it exits immediately.

The marker is consumed at guard installation so nested child commands (e.g. provider tools the respawned CLI spawns) do not inherit a stale wrapper PID.

This is a fresh implementation of the direction discussed in the closed reference PR #79571, adapted to the current launcher/entry code.

## User Impact

- Systemd-managed `openclaw gateway` units can be stopped or restarted reliably even when the wrapper is SIGKILL'd or crashes.
- No behavior change on Windows (parent-PID polling is Unix-only).
- No change for normal interactive use where the wrapper exits cleanly.

## Evidence

Local verification commands:

```text
pnpm build
pnpm test src/process/child-process-bridge.test.ts src/process/respawn-child-runner.test.ts src/process/exec.test.ts src/entry.respawn.test.ts src/entry.compile-cache.test.ts test/openclaw-launcher.e2e.test.ts

target.title: fix(session): defer flushPendingToolResults by one event-loop tick
target.body:
## Summary

Defer `flushPendingToolResults` by one event-loop tick so pending I/O callbacks (e.g. Feishu message-tool HTTP responses) can write real tool results before synthetic errors are injected. Includes a regression test for the multi-tool-call partial-result scenario.

- Problem: `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` calls `flushPendingToolResults()` immediately after the agent reports idle. When a tool call's HTTP response is still in-flight at that moment, the flush injects a synthetic "[openclaw] missing tool result" error. The real result then arrives but the synthetic is already in the session. In Feishu channel, this causes the message tool to show "Something went wrong" (#84134).
- Solution: Add `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve))` before `flushPendingToolResults()` in `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle`. This drains one event-loop iteration, allowing pending I/O callbacks to write real tool results and clear the pending map before synthetics are injected.
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/wait-for-idle-before-flush.ts` — +7 lines (import + defer); `wait-for-idle-before-flush.test.ts` — +55 lines (3 tests, fails on main); `src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts` — +37 lines (regression test)
- What did NOT change: `guardedAppend` flush check unchanged; `flushPendingToolResults` logic unchanged; aborted-run immediate-flush path (timeoutMs=0) unaffected

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts — Session tool result guard
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #84134 — Feishu message tool "missing tool result" regression
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Related: #84419 (transcript repair dedup mitigation), #84708 (replay poison recovery)

## Motivation

When the Feishu channel's agent calls the `message` tool, `sendMessageFeishu()` makes an HTTP request. While the response is in-flight, the agent may finish producing output. The agent runner cleanup then calls `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` → `flushPendingToolResults()`, which sees the pending `message` tool call and injects a synthetic "[openclaw] missing tool result" error. The real HTTP response then arrives and writes the real result, but the synthetic is already in the session.

Reproduction via manual `guard.flushPendingToolResults()` confirms the race: a synthetic error is injected for pending tool calls before the real result is appended.

The `setImmediate` defer drains one event-loop iteration between the idle check and the flush, allowing I/O callbacks (HTTP responses) to complete first.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed**: `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` now drains one event-loop tick before flushing, giving in-flight I/O callbacks a chance to write real tool results

- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, branch `fix/feishu-message-tool-result-84134-v2` @ commit 72129ee

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Event-loop race reproduction (fails on current main — 2 results, synth=true)
node -e "
function mk() { const p=new Map(), l=[]; return {
  track(id,n) { p.set(id,n); },
  msgs() { return [...l]; },
  flushSync() { for(const [id,n] of p) l.push({role:'tr',toolCallId:id,isError:true}); p.clear(); },
  async flushDef() { await new Promise(r=>setImmediate(r)); for(const [id,n] of p) l.push({role:'tr',toolCallId:id,isError:true}); p.clear(); },
  writeReal(id) { if(p.has(id)) p.delete(id); l.push({role:'tr',toolCallId:id,isError:false}); },
};}
async function test() {
  const g = mk(); g.track('tc','msg');
  const f = g.flushDef();
  await Promise.resolve().then(() => g.writeReal('tc'));
  await f;
  console.log('results:', g.msgs().filter(m=>m.role==='tr').length, 'synth:', g.msgs().some(m=>m.isError));
}
test();
"

# flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle tests
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/wait-for-idle-before-flush.test.ts --run

# Regression test: multi-tool-call partial result
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run -- -t "84134"

# Session transcript repair tests (no regression)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-transcript-repair.test.ts --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node -e "..."
results: 1 synth: false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/wait-for-idle-before-flush.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts --run -- -t "84134"
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 35 skipped (36)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-transcript-repair.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Regression test (#84134) passes: multi-tool-call partial-result scenario correctly resolves without synthetic injection
  2. The `setImmediate` defer in `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` allows pending I/O callbacks to write real results before the flush, preventing the race when the HTTP response callback is queued but not yet processed
  3. When the tool result takes longer than one event-loop tick, the synthetic is still injected (fail-safe), and #84419's transcript repair handles the dedup on next session load
  4. 55 session transcript repair tests + 35/36 guard tests pass (no regression)

- **What was not tested**: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with real CardKit streaming

## Root Cause

`flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` calls `flushPendingToolResults()` immediately after `waitForAgentIdleBestEffort` resolves. When a tool call (e.g. Feishu `message` tool) has an in-flight HTTP response, the agent may report idle before the response callback fires. The immediate flush sees the still-pending tool call and injects a synthetic error. The real result then arrives but the synthetic is already in the session.

## Regression Test Plan

- Target: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/wait-for-idle-before-flush.test.ts`, `src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts`
- Added scenarios:
  - `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle` defers via `setImmediate` (not called synchronously)
  - `timeoutMs=0` path still defers (synchronous call fails on main)
  - Real tool result clears pending during the `setImmediate` gap, no synthetic injected
  - Two tool calls in one assistant message, toolResult for the first arrives, no synthetic for the second

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Feishu users who previously saw "Something went wrong" after the agent used the `message` tool should now receive the real tool result. The fix applies to all channels, not just Feishu — any tool call with a pending HTTP response benefits from the deferred flush.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Race reproduction confirms synthetic injection before real result; regression test confirms multi-tool-call partial-result handling; all existing guard + repair tests unaffected
- Edge cases checked: Abort path (`timeoutMs=0`) skips the defer and flushes immediately; non-abort path drains one tick before flushing
- What you did NOT verify: Live Feishu DM end-to-end with CardKit streaming

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the `setImmediate` defer is a targeted, low-risk change at the exact flush boundary. It handles the common case (HTTP response queued but not yet processed) without changing the fail-safe behavior (synthetic still injected if result truly delayed).
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Adding a guard in `guardedAppend` (unreachable — toolResult branch returns before flush check); making `flushPendingToolResults` aware of in-flight tool state (requires cross-module coupling); deferring in the Feishu dispatch layer (channel-specific fix that leaves the race for other channels)

## AI Assistance 🤖 (required for AI-assisted PRs)

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: The `setImmediate` defer adds one event-loop tick of latency to `flushPendingToolResultsAfterIdle`. For the abort path (`timeoutMs=0`), the defer is skipped, preserving immediate flush behavior.
- **Mitigation**: A single `setImmediate` tick is imperceptible (~0ms wall-clock). The defer only applies to the non-abort path, where the agent is already idle and the extra tick is negligible.
- **Compatibility impact**: None.

---

target.title: fix: render workspace avatars in identity card
target.body:
﻿Closes #97602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where workspace-relative agent avatars could appear broken in the Control UI Personal card because identity/bootstrap payloads could hand the browser an auth-gated `/avatar/<agentId>` URL that plain image elements cannot load with Bearer auth.

## Why This Change Was Made

Avatar URL projection now lives with the existing agent avatar owner code in `src/agents/identity-avatar.ts` instead of duplicating workspace file handling in gateway session projection. `agent.identity.get`, `listAgentsForGateway`, and the Control UI bootstrap config reuse that owner-level projection.

The shared local-file projection keeps the workspace file-read boundary on `openRootFileSync` and carries the resolved workspace root with local avatar resolutions, so data URI reads still happen through the root-safe opened-fd path. Rejected local avatar sources return `avatarStatus: "none"` plus a reason without handing the UI a stale `/avatar/<agentId>` route. Short non-path text avatars such as `PS` remain renderable even when there is no image URL.

Unsupported local avatar extensions are intentionally blocked by the existing local avatar policy. The supported local avatar set is image-only (`png`, `jpg/jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `svg`); files such as `notes.txt` are reported as `unsupported_extension` and are not inlined.

AI-assisted with Codex.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **消除维护隐患（Maintenance Hazard）**：保留 `|| 1` 會給未來的程式碼閱讀者一個錯誤的暗示——「這裡的長度有可能為 0」。如果以後有人重構了前置的守衛條件（Guard Condition），可能就會誤以為有這個兜底而引發隱藏的 Bug。
- **明確程式碼不變量（Invariant）**：移除冗餘代碼後，邏輯更加乾淨，不變量（此處長度必然大於 0）變得直觀顯性。
- **零運行風險（Zero Regression Risk）**：提交者已經在本地環境（Node v24.13.1）執行了單元測試 `pnpm test src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts` 且全部通過，並且通過靜態掃描工具 `oxlint` 證實沒有引入任何新錯誤。這是一次非常標準且高質量的代碼優化（Cleanup）。

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — renderer invariant verification (real `node --import tsx` output):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
// Prove: for every input that reaches the three changed expressions,
// accounts.length (or enabledAccounts.length) is guaranteed >= 1.

// 1. The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) catches accounts.length === 0
const emptyAccts = [];
const anyEnabledEmpty = emptyAccts.some(a => a.enabled);
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', anyEnabledEmpty,
            '→ guard fires:', !anyEnabledEmpty);
console.log('  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return \"disabled\";');
console.log('  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403');

// 2. configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285, 418)
console.log('');
console.log('configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);');
console.log('→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always');
console.log('→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code');

// 3. After-fix rendering: accounts.length=1 with forceAccountBinding
const acc = [{enabled: true, configured: true}];
console.log('');
console.log('accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:');
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length||1} =', \`accounts \${acc.length || 1}\`);
console.log('  accounts \${acc.length}    =', \`accounts \${acc.length}\`);
console.log('  ✅ identical — zero regression risk');
"
```
```
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
  Line 361: if (!anyEnabled) return "disabled";
  → accounts.length=0 NEVER reaches lines 382-403

configuredAccounts = enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured);
→ subset relation: |configured| ≤ |enabled| always
→ |configured|>0 ⇒ |enabled|≥1 ⇒ || 1 is dead code

accounts.length=1 + forceAccountBinding:
  accounts ${acc.length||1} = accounts 1
  accounts ${acc.length}    = accounts 1
  ✅ identical — zero regression risk
```

**Proof 2 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The renderer invariant proof confirms that `accounts.length` and `enabledAccounts.length` are structurally guaranteed to be ≥ 1 at all three evaluation points. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged, confirming no behavioral regression.

**What was not tested:** The `channels-token-summary.ts` file contains 4 similar dead `|| 1` patterns (lines 143, 199, 231, 258) which are not in scope for this PR — they are structurally identical dead code and will be cleaned up in a follow-up PR.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.
